fields.features_heading: What the Front Desk Gets Back
fields.features_subheading: Each signed consent comes back with the details a clipboard copy leaves out.
fields.feature_1:
Signed on a phone before the visit starts

Send the link with the appointment reminder, or post a code at the front window. Patients read and sign on their own phone, and the signature lands on their record with the time.
fields.feature_2:
The exact wording each patient agreed to

Number each version of your consent text. Every signed record keeps that number, so a signature from March still points to March's wording after you rewrite a clause in May.
fields.feature_3:
Privacy notice receipt in the same link

Put the notice of privacy practices before the signature and ask the patient to confirm they received it. The acknowledgment is dated and saved with the consent as one record.
fields.feature_4:
Each treatment accepted or declined

List the treatments your consent covers, such as injections or manual therapy. A patient can say no to one and sign for the rest, and the declined item shows on the schedule.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts that carry a link, not the answers

Send an email or Slack message when a form is in. The alert says a consent was signed and links to the record, and every answer stays in a database you own, never in the message.
fields.feature_6:
Code to run inside your own systems

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Run the consent form inside your patient portal or intake app, and keep editing it there without a rebuild from scratch.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is eight clinic and agency PDFs (an emergency physicians' group, two hospital systems, a medical group, a university, a state agency, a health center, a malpractice insurer's samples): one page of clauses and a signature line, handed over at the front desk. None shows when the patient signed, which wording they agreed to, or who still has to sign. This page builds the general consent signed on the patient's phone before the visit, with the form version and signature time on every record, the privacy notice acknowledgment on the same link, treatments a patient can decline one by one, and a re-sign date the clinic sets.
tab_stories: At Cedar Point Urgent Care, patients scan a code at the window and sign version 3 of the consent from the waiting room, and the check-in list shows 1 of 12 morning patients still unsigned.

Willow Street Counseling sends its consent with intake 2 days before a first session, the client initials the cancellation and confidentiality sections, and the therapist gets an email that a form is in, with a link.
At Ridgeline Physical Therapy a new patient agrees to exercise and manual therapy but declines dry needling, and the declined technique shows next to her name on the therapist's schedule.
Brookside Family Medicine sets its own rule that consent is re-signed every 12 months, so a patient whose last signature is 13 months old gets the current version to sign before check-in.

claims_to_source: HIPAA: a covered entity may obtain consent to use or disclose PHI for treatment, payment or health care operations (45 CFR 164.506(b)(1))
HIPAA: consent under 164.506(b) does not replace an authorization where 164.508 requires one (45 CFR 164.506(b)(2))
HIPAA: a direct-treatment provider makes a good faith effort to obtain written acknowledgment of the privacy notice, except in an emergency (45 CFR 164.520(c)(2)(ii))
HIPAA: a direct-treatment provider gives the privacy notice no later than the first service delivery (45 CFR 164.520(c)(2)(i))
For routine interventions unlikely to cause harm, circumstances are typically considered to imply consent (Merck Manual)
Informed consent covers the potential harms and benefits of treatments (Merck Manual)
